rows.col_1: GET https://developer.api.autodesk.com/cost/v1/containers/:containerId/cost-items/:costItemId/sub-cost-items
User context required
data:read
JSON

Must be Bearer <token>, where <token> is a three-legged access token obtained via an Authorization Code flow or a Secure Service Account (SSA) flow.
The SSA flow is designed for headless server-to-server operations. While it functions like a two-legged flow (no user interaction), it is classified as three-legged because it preserves user context.

Specifies the region where the project data resides.
By default, the request is routed automatically. However, specifying the region can improve performance by avoiding lookup overhead.
Possible values: country or region codes such as US or EMEA. For the full list of supported regions, see the Forma Regions page.
To verify your project’s region, refer to the Working with BIM 360 Services in Different Regions section on the API Basics page.
The ID of the project (the container ID is the same as the project ID). To obtain the project ID, see GET projects.

A cost item ID to retrieve sub cost items for one cost item in a single request. The response includes all sub cost items associated with the specified cost item. Cost items do not have parent-child relationships, but sub cost items can be structured under other sub cost items. To find the cost item ID, call GET cost-items.

The type of the value to break down.
Possible values: estimated, proposed, submitted, approved, committed

The number of records to skip before returning results. Used together with limit to paginate through results, where offset specifies the starting point and limit specifies the number of records to return.
The maximum number of records returned per page. Default: 100. A page may contain fewer records than the limit if there are fewer matching items or if it is the last page of results.
Defines the sort order for the results. Each attribute can be sorted in asc (default) or desc order. For example, sort=name desc sorts the results by name in descending order.
The request was successful, returning the retrieved sub cost items.

Contains pagination information when data is returned page by page.
The maximum number of records returned in the response.
The number of records skipped before returning the page of results.
The total number of records that matched the request criteria.

The URL for the next request to retrieve the next page of results. Max length: 2000.
Max length: 2000
A list of sub cost items associated with the requested cost items.
The unique ID of the sub cost item.
The unique ID of the parent sub cost item. A sub cost item has a parent Id when it is part of a hierarchical cost structure. Root sub cost items do not have a parent ID.

The classification of the sub cost item that indicates its role in cost tracking and approval workflows. Possible values: estimated, proposed, submitted, approved, committed.
Max length: 255
The ID of the cost item to which the sub cost item belongs.

The identifier for the sub cost item. If copied from another model, for example, a Contract SOV, it inherits the code. Otherwise, it is manually assigned.
Max length: 255

The position of the sub cost item relative to its sibling sub cost items. If a new sub cost item is assigned a position that already exists, the system shifts existing items downward to maintain order.

The name of the sub cost item.
Max length: 1024
The planned number of units allocated for the sub cost item.
The recorded input quantity, typically used in performance tracking. For example, in labor tracking, inputQuantity represents man-hours utilized.
The price per individual unit of the sub cost item.

The unit of measurement for the sub cost item. This value is configured in the Unit of measure settings for the project. Common units include ea (Each), gal (Gallon), and various volume, length, and time measurements.
Max length: 1024
The total value of the sub cost item, calculated as quantity * unitPrice.
The date and time that the item was created, in ISO 8601 format.
The date and time that the item was last updated, in ISO 8601 format.
